# Random Design

Preserve the supplied content, facts, prices and intended voice. Use the visual specification to decide typography, palette, layout, material and the role of illustrations.

## Choose the entry point

- **Content-led complete design:** first inspect the actual examples at https://xingchenyd.github.io/random-design/showcase/. Use MCP list_reference_styles and generate_reference_briefs, or the browser picker https://xingchenyd.github.io/random-design/reference/. The returned brief is an implementation specification, NOT a finished page. Read [reference workflow](references/reference-library.md) before executing it.


- **Named style:** use MCP `list_presets` to resolve the ID and `get_preset` to obtain the fixed design. In a checkout, run `node src/cli.js list-presets` or `node src/cli.js preset --style new-chinese --out <new-directory>`. A named preset can be reused without advancing random history.
- **Explore variations:** call MCP `generate_directions` or run `node src/cli.js generate --out <new-directory>`. Pass the same content to each preview. Use a supplied seed if the user requests repeatability and carry over the caller's random history when available. Use `direction` to constrain variations to a named style.
- **Browser only:** open https://xingchenyd.github.io/random-design/presets/ for the fixed styles or https://xingchenyd.github.io/random-design/ for both modes. Select the style in the studio and download JSON, HTML or PPTX. See [integrations](references/integrations.md) for available clients.

## Apply the direction

Use `render_design` for a preview, CSS, SVG and a brief. The CLI and studio also generate a six-slide PowerPoint specimen. Adapt the layout and illustration to the user's subject. For example, keep the New Chinese Style's vertical short title and circular composition while replacing the sample coffee illustration if it has no role in the new content.

Do not turn every request into three generic cards or reuse a coffee illustration for unrelated subjects. Establish a type hierarchy and content grid first. Decoration needs a role: navigation, grouping, data encoding, branding or relevant illustration.\n\nFor these 21 styles, use the [material and reference guide](references/materials.md) to retain the lighting, surfaces and layout that make each style recognizable.

Check the actual page at its intended viewport or render the final slides. Review the title hierarchy, focal point, content fit and readability. Preserve native text and data when editing PPTX. Its complex illustration is an SVG image and some website effects have a PowerPoint-specific treatment.

Save the selected `design.json` and the project version. v0.3 can read v0.2 specifications and histories. Use the corresponding release for the older seed-to-design mapping. Keep user-selected constraints if candidate generation exhausts its budget and explain which constraint caused the conflict.

# hash-design：用外部随机打破默认审美

LLM 做页面会塌缩到众数审美。这个 Skill 的做法是：**风格不由你选**。先用真随机哈希掷骰，经过固定、可复现的决策树映射成 5 个彼此不同的设计方向（brief），你只负责**忠实执行** brief，把选择权交还给用户。

## 何时使用

- 用户要做/重做一个网页、落地页、一页站、活动页、作品集首页、海报式页面、UI 视觉稿。
- 用户说"要有设计感""别像 AI 做的""给我几个方向"。
- 不适用：纯后端、已有严格设计系统且用户要求遵守的改动（此时只用 `critique_page` 自检即可）。

## 前置条件

- 已连接 MCP server `hash-design`（工具：`roll_designs`、`get_brief`、`list_branches`、`get_branch`、`critique_page`、`build_compare_page`）。
- 没有 MCP 时用 CLI 等价替代：`npx -y hash-design roll …`、`hash-design critique …`、`hash-design compare …`（见文末对照表）。

## 工作流（严格按顺序）

### 0. 收集事实

向用户要（或从仓库/上下文里找）**事实清单**：名称、地址、时间、价格、产品、联系方式、真实卖点。页面上只能出现这些事实。缺的就在页面里留"【待补：…】"，**绝不编造**数字、评价、客户、奖项。

### 1. 掷骰（不要自己挑风格）

调用 `roll_designs`：

```json
{ "subject": "第四巷面包店 一页站", "facts": ["…", "…"], "count": 5, "out_dir": "design/hash-design" }
```

- **不要传 `seed`**。seed 只用于复现示例；真实使用必须用系统随机。
- 用户的硬约束才写进约束：`light_only` / `dark_only` / `reduced_motion` / `brand_colors`（品牌色，最多 2 个）/ `families` / `include_branches` / `exclude_branches`。不要为了"安全"擅自加约束。
- **不要因为不喜欢结果而重掷。** 只有用户要求时才重掷。

### 2. 冻结 brief

`out_dir` 会写出 `roll.json`、`ROLL.md` 和 `briefs/01-<branch>.md … 05-<branch>.md`。从这一刻起 brief 是**冻结的规格**：

- 字体、色值、版式结构、首屏锚点（anchor）、密度、动效、母题、材质、文案语气（voice）、变数（twist）都按 brief 执行。
- 不允许"顺手优化"成你习惯的样子（换成 Inter、加渐变、加圆角阴影卡片、把首屏改成居中双按钮……）。
- 需要复现某个 brief：`get_brief`，传 `ref` 和**同样的约束**。

### 3. 逐个渲染 5 个独立 HTML 预览

对每个 brief **单独**做一个预览，保存为 `design/hash-design/previews/<与 brief 同名>.html`，例如 `previews/01-supermarket-circular.html`。

独立性要求（这是方法能生效的关键）：

- 做第 N 个时，**只看第 N 份 brief**；不要参考前面预览的代码，不要复用 CSS，不要统一组件。能开子 Agent 就每个预览开一个独立子 Agent，只给它那一份 brief + 事实。
- 每个预览是**单文件**：内联 `<style>`，用 brief 里的 Google Fonts `<link>`，粘贴 brief 的 `tokens.css` 并只用这些变量取色；不用 Tailwind CDN、不用 UI 框架、不引入图标库。
- 首屏必须是 brief 的 **anchor**，结构按 **layout.structure** 的顺序；文案按 **voice** 写；**twist** 要看得出来。
- 图片：没有真实素材就不用照片，用排版、色块、自绘 SVG、brief 母题完成视觉。
- 必须响应式（至少 390px 手机宽度可读），`<html lang>`、`<meta viewport>` 齐全，尊重 `prefers-reduced-motion`。
- 文件顶部写注释：`<!-- hash-design #N · <branch-id> · ref <ref> -->`。

### 4. 自检每个预览

对每个预览调用 `critique_page`：

```json
{ "path": "design/hash-design/previews/01-supermarket-circular.html", "roll_path": "design/hash-design/roll.json", "pick": 1 }
```

- 所有 **critical / major** 必须修掉；minor 尽量修，保留的要能说出理由。
- `adherence`（对 brief 的遵守度）应 ≥ 80。低于就是你偏离了 brief，回去对照 brief 改。
- 静态检查抓不到一切：再自己对照 brief 的「交付前自检」清单过一遍。

### 5. 并排对比页，然后停下

调用 `build_compare_page`（`{"roll_path": "design/hash-design/roll.json"}`），得到 `compare.html`：5 个预览缩放后并排，带分支名、配色色块、字体、语气、变数，支持桌面/手机切换和单张放大。

把 compare.html 的路径（能打开就直接打开）交给用户，用一两句话概括每个方向的差异，然后**停下，等用户回复编号**。不要替用户选，不要说"我推荐 #3"，除非用户明确问你意见。

### 6. 按选中的 brief 落地正式页面

- 只读选中的那一份 brief（及其预览）。预览可以作为起点，但正式页面要把**全部事实**组织进去，补齐所有区块、交互和移动端。
- 仍然遵守 brief 的全部 token 和全局禁令；用户要求的修改优先于 brief，但不要借机回到默认审美。
- 用户如果明确要求混搭（"#2 的版式 + #4 的配色"），照做，并在页面注释里写明来源 ref。

### 7. 最终自检并交付

对正式页面调用 `critique_page`（带 `roll_path` + `pick` 或 `brief_ref`），修到没有 critical/major。交付时说明：用了哪个 ref、做了哪些取舍、还有哪些"待补"事实。

## 硬性规则

1. 风格来自骰子，不来自你。你的品味只用于**执行质量**：对齐、节奏、细节、可读性。
2. 一个 brief 一个独立预览；预览之间不共享代码。
3. 只用事实；不编造社会证明。
4. 全局禁令高于一切（见下方，自动生成，与数据同步）。
5. 展示对比页后必须停下等用户选择。

# hash-design：用外部随机打破默认审美

LLM 做页面会塌缩到众数审美。这个 Skill 的做法是：**风格不由你选**。先用真随机哈希掷骰，经过固定、可复现的决策树映射成 5 个彼此不同的设计方向（brief），你只负责**忠实执行** brief，把选择权交还给用户。

## 何时使用

- 用户要做/重做一个网页、落地页、一页站、活动页、作品集首页、海报式页面、UI 视觉稿。
- 用户说"要有设计感""别像 AI 做的""给我几个方向"。
- 不适用：纯后端、已有严格设计系统且用户要求遵守的改动（此时只用 `critique_page` 自检即可）。

## 前置条件

- 已连接 MCP server `hash-design`（工具：`roll_designs`、`get_brief`、`list_branches`、`get_branch`、`critique_page`、`build_compare_page`）。
- 没有 MCP 时用 CLI 等价替代：`npx -y hash-design roll …`、`hash-design critique …`、`hash-design compare …`（见文末对照表）。

## 工作流（严格按顺序）

### 0. 收集事实

向用户要（或从仓库/上下文里找）**事实清单**：名称、地址、时间、价格、产品、联系方式、真实卖点。页面上只能出现这些事实。缺的就在页面里留"【待补：…】"，**绝不编造**数字、评价、客户、奖项。

### 1. 掷骰（不要自己挑风格）

调用 `roll_designs`：

```json
{ "subject": "第四巷面包店 一页站", "facts": ["…", "…"], "count": 5, "out_dir": "design/hash-design" }
```

- **不要传 `seed`**。seed 只用于复现示例；真实使用必须用系统随机。
- 用户的硬约束才写进约束：`light_only` / `dark_only` / `reduced_motion` / `brand_colors`（品牌色，最多 2 个）/ `families` / `include_branches` / `exclude_branches`。不要为了"安全"擅自加约束。
- **不要因为不喜欢结果而重掷。** 只有用户要求时才重掷。

### 2. 冻结 brief

`out_dir` 会写出 `roll.json`、`ROLL.md` 和 `briefs/01-<branch>.md … 05-<branch>.md`。从这一刻起 brief 是**冻结的规格**：

- 字体、色值、版式结构、首屏锚点（anchor）、密度、动效、母题、材质、文案语气（voice）、变数（twist）都按 brief 执行。
- 不允许"顺手优化"成你习惯的样子（换成 Inter、加渐变、加圆角阴影卡片、把首屏改成居中双按钮……）。
- 需要复现某个 brief：`get_brief`，传 `ref` 和**同样的约束**。

### 3. 逐个渲染 5 个独立 HTML 预览

对每个 brief **单独**做一个预览，保存为 `design/hash-design/previews/<与 brief 同名>.html`，例如 `previews/01-supermarket-circular.html`。

独立性要求（这是方法能生效的关键）：

- 做第 N 个时，**只看第 N 份 brief**；不要参考前面预览的代码，不要复用 CSS，不要统一组件。能开子 Agent 就每个预览开一个独立子 Agent，只给它那一份 brief + 事实。
- 每个预览是**单文件**：内联 `<style>`，用 brief 里的 Google Fonts `<link>`，粘贴 brief 的 `tokens.css` 并只用这些变量取色；不用 Tailwind CDN、不用 UI 框架、不引入图标库。
- 首屏必须是 brief 的 **anchor**，结构按 **layout.structure** 的顺序；文案按 **voice** 写；**twist** 要看得出来。
- 图片：没有真实素材就不用照片，用排版、色块、自绘 SVG、brief 母题完成视觉。
- 必须响应式（至少 390px 手机宽度可读），`<html lang>`、`<meta viewport>` 齐全，尊重 `prefers-reduced-motion`。
- 文件顶部写注释：`<!-- hash-design #N · <branch-id> · ref <ref> -->`。

### 4. 自检每个预览

对每个预览调用 `critique_page`：

```json
{ "path": "design/hash-design/previews/01-supermarket-circular.html", "roll_path": "design/hash-design/roll.json", "pick": 1 }
```

- 所有 **critical / major** 必须修掉；minor 尽量修，保留的要能说出理由。
- `adherence`（对 brief 的遵守度）应 ≥ 80。低于就是你偏离了 brief，回去对照 brief 改。
- 静态检查抓不到一切：再自己对照 brief 的「交付前自检」清单过一遍。

### 5. 并排对比页，然后停下

调用 `build_compare_page`（`{"roll_path": "design/hash-design/roll.json"}`），得到 `compare.html`：5 个预览缩放后并排，带分支名、配色色块、字体、语气、变数，支持桌面/手机切换和单张放大。

把 compare.html 的路径（能打开就直接打开）交给用户，用一两句话概括每个方向的差异，然后**停下，等用户回复编号**。不要替用户选，不要说"我推荐 #3"，除非用户明确问你意见。

### 6. 按选中的 brief 落地正式页面

- 只读选中的那一份 brief（及其预览）。预览可以作为起点，但正式页面要把**全部事实**组织进去，补齐所有区块、交互和移动端。
- 仍然遵守 brief 的全部 token 和全局禁令；用户要求的修改优先于 brief，但不要借机回到默认审美。
- 用户如果明确要求混搭（"#2 的版式 + #4 的配色"），照做，并在页面注释里写明来源 ref。

### 7. 最终自检并交付

对正式页面调用 `critique_page`（带 `roll_path` + `pick` 或 `brief_ref`），修到没有 critical/major。交付时说明：用了哪个 ref、做了哪些取舍、还有哪些"待补"事实。

## 硬性规则

1. 风格来自骰子，不来自你。你的品味只用于**执行质量**：对齐、节奏、细节、可读性。
2. 一个 brief 一个独立预览；预览之间不共享代码。
3. 只用事实；不编造社会证明。
4. 全局禁令高于一切（见下方，自动生成，与数据同步）。
5. 展示对比页后必须停下等用户选择。

Los `package.json` están listos para publicarse y CI ejecuta `npm pack --dry-run`, pero `npx hash-design` y `npx hash-design-mcp` no funcionarán hasta que haya una versión publicada. --- ## Qué hace hash-design Pídele a un LLM "una página bonita" y casi siempre acabará en la misma estética predominante: Inter, un degradado de morado a azul, un titular centrado con dos botones, tres tarjetas de características idénticas, glassmorphism, iconos emoji y textos como _Unlock_, _Seamless_, _Supercharge_. La razón es sencilla: siempre que el modelo puede elegir, escoge lo más común de sus datos de entrenamiento. hash-design no le pide al modelo que tenga mejor gusto. **Le quita la decisión**: | Paso | Qué pasa | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Tirada** | Genera cinco hashes a partir de la aleatoriedad del sistema (`crypto.randomBytes(32)` → SHA-256). | | **Mapeo** | Asigna cada hash, mediante un **árbol de decisión fijo y reproducible**, a una dirección concreta: género de diseño, maquetación, combinación de fuentes, paleta hex, densidad, movimiento, motivo, ancla de la primera pantalla, escala tipográfica, superficie, voz de redacción y un "giro" (twist). | | **Congelación** | Congela cada dirección como un **brief** con tokens listos para pegar (enlaces de fuentes, valores hex, `tokens.css`, medidas de la retícula, política de radio/sombra), más las prohibiciones globales. | | **Render** | La única tarea del agente es **ejecutar** cada brief con fidelidad: cinco vistas previas HTML independientes y una página comparativa lado a lado. Después **se detiene y espera a que elijas un número**. | | **Página final** | Cuando eliges, el agente construye la página final a partir de ese brief y la revisa con `critique_page`. | Se trata de una restricción aleatoria externa que rompe la estética por defecto del modelo. No tiene nada que ver con cachés KV ni con la temperatura de muestreo. El gusto del modelo se invierte en la calidad de ejecución (alineación, ritmo, detalle, legibilidad), no en elegir un estilo. Se distribuye como una **Agent Skill** (cuándo y en qué orden ejecutar el flujo), un **servidor MCP** (stdio, seis herramientas), una **CLI** y una **biblioteca TypeScript**, todo en este repositorio. ## Inicio rápido ### Pídeselo a tu agente Abre Claude Code o Cursor en el proyecto que quieres diseñar y pega: ```text Instala hash-design desde https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design (todavía no está en npm): clónalo en ~/hash-design, compílalo y, siguiendo los pasos de "Instalación manual" de su README.es.md, instala su skill en este proyecto y registra su servidor MCP para este agente. ``` El agente clona y compila este repositorio, copia la Skill en `.claude/skills/` o `.cursor/skills/` de tu proyecto y registra el servidor MCP (`claude mcp add` en Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` en Cursor). 01 · Swiss grid		 ¿Qué agentes pueden usarlo? La Skill se instala en Claude Code (`.claude/skills/`) y en Cursor (`.cursor/skills/`). El servidor MCP habla stdio, así que cualquier cliente MCP puede arrancarlo; [Instalación manual](#instalación-manual) muestra Claude Code, Cursor y Claude Desktop. Sin la Skill, un agente puede llamar a las herramientas, pero nada le indica que renderice las vistas previas por separado y se detenga hasta que elijas.
¿Está en npm? Todavía no. Los `package.json` están listos para publicarse y CI ejecuta `npm pack --dry-run`, pero por ahora hay que instalar desde el código fuente. Cuando se publique, funcionarán `npx -y hash-design-mcp` y `npx -y hash-design`.

> [!IMPORTANT] > hash-design은 **아직 npm에 배포하지 않았습니다**. 소스([qybaihe/hash-design](https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design))에서 설치하세요. `package.json`은 배포 가능한 상태이고 CI에서 `npm pack --dry-run`을 실행하지만, 릴리스 전까지 `npx hash-design`과 `npx hash-design-mcp`는 동작하지 않습니다. --- ## hash-design가 하는 일 LLM에게 "멋진 페이지"를 만들어 달라고 하면 거의 언제나 똑같은 최빈값 미학으로 수렴합니다. Inter 폰트, 보라에서 파랑으로 넘어가는 그라데이션, 가운데 정렬된 헤드라인과 버튼 두 개, 똑같이 생긴 기능 카드 세 장, 글래스모피즘, 이모지 아이콘, 그리고 _Unlock_, _Seamless_, _Supercharge_ 같은 문구까지. 이유는 간단합니다. 모델은 선택권이 주어질 때마다 학습 데이터에서 가장 흔한 것을 고르기 때문입니다. hash-design은 모델에게 더 나은 안목을 요구하지 않습니다. 대신 **선택권을 빼앗습니다**: | 단계 | 하는 일 | | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **롤** | 시스템 난수로 해시 다섯 개를 뽑습니다(`crypto.randomBytes(32)` → SHA-256). | | **매핑** | 각 해시를 **고정되고 재현 가능한 결정 트리**에 통과시켜 구체적인 방향으로 매핑합니다. 디자인 장르, 레이아웃, 폰트 조합, hex 팔레트, 밀도, 모션, 모티프, 첫 화면 앵커, 타입 스케일, 표면, 카피 보이스, 그리고 "트위스트" 하나가 정해집니다. | | **고정** | 각 방향을 **브리프**로 고정합니다. 브리프에는 바로 붙여 넣을 수 있는 토큰(폰트 링크, hex 값, `tokens.css`, 그리드 수치, 모서리 반경/그림자 정책)과 전역 금지 규칙이 담깁니다. | | **렌더링** | 에이전트가 할 일은 각 브리프를 충실히 **실행하는 것**뿐입니다. 독립된 HTML 프리뷰 다섯 개와 나란히 비교하는 페이지를 만든 다음, **멈추고 사용자가 번호를 고를 때까지 기다립니다**. | | **최종 페이지** | 번호를 고르면 에이전트는 그 브리프로 최종 페이지를 만들고 `critique_page`로 검사합니다. | 이것은 모델의 기본 미학을 깨뜨리는 외부의 무작위 제약입니다. KV 캐시나 샘플링 temperature와는 아무 관련이 없습니다. 모델의 안목은 스타일을 고르는 데가 아니라 실행 품질(정렬, 리듬, 디테일, 가독성)에 쓰입니다. 구성은 **Agent Skill**(언제, 어떤 순서로 이 흐름을 돌릴지), **MCP 서버**(stdio, 도구 6개), **CLI**, **TypeScript 라이브러리** 네 가지이며, 모두 이 저장소에 있습니다. ## 빠른 시작 ### 에이전트에게 맡기기 페이지를 만들 프로젝트에서 Claude Code나 Cursor를 열고 다음을 붙여 넣으세요: ```text https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design 에서 hash-design을 설치해 줘 (아직 npm에 없음). ~/hash-design에 clone해서 빌드한 다음, README.ko.md의 "직접 설치" 절차대로 skill을 이 프로젝트에 설치하고 이 에이전트용 MCP 서버를 등록해 줘. ``` 에이전트가 이 저장소를 clone해 빌드하고, Skill을 프로젝트의 `.claude/skills/` 또는 `.cursor/skills/`에 복사한 뒤 MCP 서버를 등록합니다(Claude Code는 `claude mcp add`, Cursor는 `.cursor/mcp.json`). 끝나면 새 세션을 시작해 둘 다 불러오게 한 다음 [사용법](#사용법)으로 넘어가세요. 명령을 직접 실행하려면 아래 절차를 따르세요. ### 직접 설치 Node.js ≥ 20이 필요합니다(개발용으로는 `.nvmrc`에 22가 고정되어 있습니다). ```bash git clone https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design.git ~/hash-design cd ~/hash-design && npm install && npm run build # CLI entry: ~/hash-design/packages/core/dist/bin.js # MCP server entry: ~/hash-design/packages/mcp/dist/bin.js ``` **Skill.** Skill은 에이전트에게 언제 hash-design을 써야 하는지, MCP 도구를 어떤 순서로 호출할지, 프리뷰를 어떻게 서로 독립적으로 렌더링할지, 언제 반드시 멈춰야 하는지를 알려 줍니다. ```bash # 프로젝트에 설치 (.claude/skills와 .cursor/skills 양쪽에 기록) node ~/hash-design/packages/core/dist/bin.js skill install --target both --dir /path/to/your/project # 홈 디렉터리에 설치 (모든 프로젝트에서 사용 가능) node ~/hash-design/packages/core/dist/bin.js skill install --target claude --global ``` 또는 [`skills/hash-design/SKILL.md`](skills/hash-design/SKILL.md)를 `.claude/skills/hash-design/SKILL.md`(Claude Code)나 `.cursor/skills/hash-design/SKILL.md`(Cursor)에 직접 복사하세요. 이 저장소에는 두 사본이 모두 들어 있으며, 테스트가 두 사본이 원본과 똑같이 유지되도록 확인합니다. Skill 본문은 중국어로 작성되어 있고, description에는 영어 트리거 문구가 들어 있습니다. **MCP 서버.** `packages/mcp/dist/bin.js`를 에이전트에 등록합니다. 셸에서는 `~/hash-design`이 절대 경로로 펼쳐지지만, JSON 파일에는 절대 경로를 직접 적어야 합니다(아래에서는 `/ABS/PATH/hash-design`). #### Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add hash-design -- node ~/hash-design/packages/mcp/dist/bin.js ``` 또는 프로젝트 수준의 `.mcp.json`을 커밋하세요. ```json { "mcpServers": { "hash-design": { "command": "node", "args": ["/ABS/PATH/hash-design/packages/mcp/dist/bin.js"] } } } ``` #### Cursor `.cursor/mcp.json`(프로젝트) 또는 `~/.cursor/mcp.json`(전역)에 같은 구조로 작성합니다. ```json { "mcpServers": { "hash-design": { "command": "node", "args": ["/ABS/PATH/hash-design/packages/mcp/dist/bin.js"] } } } ``` #### Claude Desktop `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`(macOS) 또는 `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`(Windows)에 위와 같은 구조로 작성합니다. Claude Desktop은 프로젝트 디렉터리에서 서버를 시작하지 않으므로, `roll_designs`를 호출할 때 `out_dir`에 **절대 경로**를 넘겨야 합니다. ### 사용법 MCP 서버와 Skill을 설치했다면 에이전트에게 이렇게 요청하기만 하면 됩니다. > hash-design으로 "Fourth Lane Bakery"의 원페이지 사이트를 만들어 줘. 팩트: 화–일 7:00–19:00 영업, 월요일 휴무; 컨트리 브레드 ¥38; … 에이전트는 롤을 실행하고, 브리프를 고정하고, 프리뷰 다섯 개를 렌더링하고, `design/hash-design/compare.html`을 작성한 다음, 멈추고 사용자가 번호로 답할 때까지 기다립니다. MCP 프롬프트를 지원하는 클라이언트에서는 `hash-design` 프롬프트(인수: `subject`, `facts`, `count`)로 같은 워크플로를 시작할 수도 있습니다. ### CLI ```bash hash-design roll --subject "Fourth Lane Bakery" --facts-file facts.md --out design/hash-design # 진짜 난수 방향 5개 hash-design roll --subject "…" --light-only --brand "#c8102e" --format json # 제약 조건 지정 hash-design brief [constraints] # 브리프 재현 hash-design branches [--family craft] # 브랜치 라이브러리 hash-design branch ink-and-seal # 브랜치 하나 상세 보기 hash-design critique page.html --roll design/hash-design/roll.json --pick 3 --fail-under 80 hash-design compare --roll design/hash-design/roll.json # compare.html 작성 hash-design skill install --target both # Skill 설치 ``` 소스 체크아웃에서는 `node packages/core/dist/bin.js …`로 실행합니다(또는 저장소 루트에서 `alias hash-design="node $PWD/packages/core/dist/bin.js"`를 설정하세요). `hash-design --help`는 모든 명령을 보여 주고, `hash-design --help`(예: `hash-design roll --help`)는 해당 명령의 옵션을 출력합니다. 여기에는 제약 조건 플래그 `--light-only`, `--dark-only`, `--reduced-motion`, `--brand`, `--family`, `--include`, `--exclude`도 포함됩니다. ### 라이브러리 ```ts import { roll, renderBrief, critiquePage, reproduce, parseRef } from 'hash-design'; const r = roll({ content: { subject: 'Fourth Lane Bakery', facts: ['Closed Mondays', 'Country loaf ¥38'] } }); for (const [i, d] of r.designs.entries()) console.log(renderBrief(d, r.content, { number: i + 1 })); const design = reproduce(parseRef(r.designs[0].ref), r.constraints); const report = critiquePage({ html: '…', design }); console.log(report.score, report.adherence, report.findings); ``` 패키지가 npm에 올라가기 전까지는 소스 체크아웃에서 가져오거나(`packages/core/dist/index.js`), 체크아웃을 로컬 의존성으로 추가하세요(`npm install /ABS/PATH/hash-design/packages/core`). ### 업데이트 ```bash cd ~/hash-design && git pull && npm install && npm run build node ~/hash-design/packages/core/dist/bin.js skill install --target both --dir /path/to/your/project # refresh the copied SKILL.md ``` MCP 설정은 `packages/mcp/dist/bin.js`를 가리키므로 다시 빌드하면 서버도 갱신됩니다. 에이전트를 재시작하면 반영됩니다. `skill install`은 프로젝트의 기존 사본을 덮어씁니다. 업데이트로 브랜치 데이터가 바뀌면 이전 버전으로 롤한 ref는 그 버전이 있어야 재현됩니다([자주 묻는 질문](#자주-묻는-질문) 참고). ## 작동 방식 ```mermaid flowchart LR A[팩트 시트] --> B[roll_designs

The `package.json` files are publish-ready and `npm pack --dry-run` runs in CI, but `npx hash-design` and `npx hash-design-mcp` will not work until a release. --- ## What hash-design does Ask an LLM for "a beautiful page" and it almost always collapses into the same modal aesthetic: Inter, a purple-to-blue gradient, a centered headline with two buttons, three identical feature cards, glassmorphism, emoji icons, and copy like _Unlock_, _Seamless_, _Supercharge_. The reason is simple: whenever the model gets to choose, it picks the most common thing in its training data. hash-design does not ask the model to have better taste. It **takes the choice away**: | Step | What happens | | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Roll** | Five hashes from system randomness (`crypto.randomBytes(32)` → SHA-256). | | **Map** | A **fixed, reproducible decision tree** turns each hash into a concrete direction: design genre, layout, font pairing, hex palette, density, motion, motif, first-screen anchor, type scale, surface, copy voice and one "twist". | | **Freeze** | Each direction becomes a **brief** with paste-ready tokens (font links, hex values, `tokens.css`, grid numbers, radius/shadow policy) plus the global bans. | | **Render** | The agent's only job is to **execute** each brief faithfully: five independent HTML previews and a side-by-side compare page. Then it **stops and waits for you to pick a number**. | | **Build** | Once you pick, the agent builds the final page from that brief and checks it with `critique_page`. | This is an external random constraint that breaks the model's default aesthetic. It has nothing to do with KV caches or sampling temperature. The model's taste is spent on execution quality (alignment, rhythm, detail, legibility), not on choosing a style. It ships as an **Agent Skill** (when and in what order to run the workflow), an **MCP server** (stdio, six tools), a **CLI** and a **TypeScript library**, all in this repository. ## Quick start ### Tell your agent Open Claude Code or Cursor in the project you want to design and paste: ```text Install hash-design from https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design (it is not on npm): clone it to ~/hash-design, build it, then install its skill into this project and register its MCP server for this agent, following the "Install by hand" steps in its README. ``` The agent clones and builds this repository, copies the Skill into your project's `.claude/skills/` or `.cursor/skills/`, and registers the MCP server (`claude mcp add` in Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` in Cursor). 5 × SHA-256, true random] B --> C[Fixed decision tree
bytes → dimensions] C --> D[5 frozen briefs
briefs/01…05.md] D --> E[5 independent HTML previews
each sees only its own brief] E --> F[build_compare_page
side by side] F --> G{User picks} G --> H[Final page
from the chosen brief] H --> I[critique_page

Collisions walk forward, see below | | 2 | voice | 14 copy voices: shopkeeper chalkboard, field notes, technical manual, personal letter, timetable, almanac… | | 3 | layout | 1 of the branch's 3 layouts, with grid numbers and a top-to-bottom section sketch | | 4 | type | 1 of 3 pairings: display / body (/ mono) + CJK fonts + typesetting notes | | 5 | palette | 1 of 3 palettes: seven hex values (paper / ink / muted / accent / accent2 / rule / panel) | | 6 | density | The branch's allowed subset of airy / regular / compact / packed | | 7 | motion | 1 of 3: duration, easing and a reduced-motion policy | | 8 | motif | 1 of the branch's 3 motifs | | 9 | anchor | 1 of the branch's 3 first-screen anchors | | 10 | scale | The branch's allowed modular scales (1.125–1.618) | | 11 | surface | 1 of 3 surfaces (with CSS hints) | | 12 | twist | 16 twists, e.g. "numerals as display", "one element breaks the grid", "no button above the fold" | | 13–31 | unused | Recorded in the brief, reserved for future dimensions | - **Collisions and family spread.** Inside one roll, a hash that lands on a branch already used walks forward (+1, +2, …) to the next free branch. While some **family** (print / document / signage / screen / craft / modernist) is still unused, landing in an already-used family also counts as a collision, so a 5-roll always spans 5 different families. The number of steps is the `probe`; a ref is written `+` and reproduces on its own. - **Branch order.** Library order is mapping order. Each family's members are spread evenly around the ring, so walking forward does not funnel probability into one branch: in 5-rolls every branch appears 9–17% of the time (uniform would be 12.5%). - **Constraints filter the pools before the bytes are applied**, so constraints are part of a design's identity: `light_only`, `dark_only`, `reduced_motion`, `brand_colors` (the brand colour replaces the accent; the palette with the nearest accent hue is chosen and contrast is reported), `families`, `include_branches`, `exclude_branches`. - **Reproducible.** The same `ref`, the same constraints and the same library fingerprint always produce the same brief. Every brief records the algorithm (`hash-design/v1`) and the library fingerprint (the first 12 hex digits of a SHA-256 over the data). - **`seed` is only for reproducing examples and tests.** Real use always draws from system randomness. # 示例：二号桥单车铺 一次完整的 hash-design 运行，对象是一家开在桥洞下的单车修理铺，页面写给中文读者。店铺、人物和数字都是虚构的，事实见 [facts.md](facts.md)。 - **在线对比页**：（按 1–5 放大，D/M 切换桌面/手机） - **全部示例**： ![二号桥单车铺：5 个随机方向并排对比](screenshots/compare.png) ## 过程 1. **掷骰**：固定 seed 只是为了让示例可复现，真实使用请去掉 `--seed`。 ```bash npm run build node packages/core/dist/bin.js roll --subject "二号桥单车铺" \ --facts-file examples/bridge-two-bikes/facts.md --seed bridge-two-bikes-5 \ --out examples/bridge-two-bikes ``` MCP 等价调用是 `roll_designs { subject, facts, seed: "bridge-two-bikes-5", out_dir }`，得到的 5 个 ref 完全相同。`npm run example:roll -- bridge-two-bikes` 会按 [`scripts/examples.mjs`](../../scripts/examples.mjs) 里的登记执行同一条命令。 **为什么是 `-5`**：示例的 seed 规则是依次试 `<名字>`、`<名字>-2`、`<名字>-3`……取第一个与之前所有示例都不撞分支的。`bridge-two-bikes` 掷出了面包店用过的水墨印章，`-2` 撞了 Sluice 的终端荧光和美术馆图录，`-3` 撞了公文表格，`-4` 撞了 4 个，`-5` 是第一个干净的。这只是为了让 4 个示例互不重复；真实使用时**不要因为不喜欢结果而重掷**。 2. **冻结**：生成 [roll.json](roll.json)、[ROLL.md](ROLL.md) 和 [briefs/](briefs)。从这一刻起 brief 就是规格。 3. **渲染**：按 [Skill](../../skills/hash-design/SKILL.md) 第 3 步，5 个预览分别由 5 个**互相看不到对方**的子 Agent 完成。每个子 Agent 只读自己那一份 brief 加 facts.md，产出单文件 HTML（内联 CSS 和 SVG，没有图片也没有框架），并用 critique 加 Playwright 截图自检至少两轮。 4. **自检**：`npm run example:critique -- bridge-two-bikes`，或逐页 `hash-design critique previews/NN-*.html --roll roll.json --pick N` | # | 分支 | critique | brief 遵守度 | 保留的 minor | | --- | -------------------------- | -------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1 | 瑞士网格 swiss-grid | 96 | 100 | 章节编号 01–04、联系条目 04.1–04.5 | | 2 | 时装画册 couture-lookbook | 96 | 100 | Look 编号与页码 01–06 | | 3 | 票根 ticket-stub | 96 | 100 | 流水号 Nº 20261102 与日期戳：brief 要求流水号取自真实日期，用的是记录当天 | | 4 | 游戏说明书 game-manual | 100 | 100 | — | | 5 | 老黄历 chinese-almanac | 100 | 100 | — | 没有 critical 和 major。剩下的 minor 都是"数字不在事实里"这条检查，命中的是版式要求的编号。 5. **对比**：`hash-design compare --roll examples/bridge-two-bikes/roll.json` 生成 [compare.html](compare.html)。 6. **选号**：Skill 规定在这里停下，等用户回复编号。示例到此为止。 ## 5 个方向 ### 01 · 瑞士网格 Swiss grid `0377a498` · 版式 Numbered index · 字体 Archivo / Archivo · 配色 Tonhalle night · 语气 问答访谈 · 变数 首屏无按钮 · [brief](briefs/01-swiss-grid.md) 首屏是几何场：一组同心细线半圆就是那座桥的拱，圆心落在网格线上，一条橙色四分之一圆带被竖向网格线切断，旁边一个蓝色圆点。4 个章节（店 / 价目 / 门口 / 联系）各由一个巨大的橙色编号领起；每节末尾是一段和老陈的问答，最后以"（访谈完）"收尾。整页没有一个按钮，电话只在第 04 节以普通文字链接出现。 ### 02 · 时装画册 Couture lookbook `92818df9+1` · 版式 Look sequence · 字体 Italiana / Cormorant Garamond · 配色 Noir & champagne · 语气 田野笔记 · 变数 强调色配给 · [brief](briefs/02-couture-lookbook.md) 首屏左半边是一个约 70vh 高的香槟色 Italiana "2"，11px 的 "BRIDGE NO." 贴着它的基线，字号的极端对比本身读成"二号桥"；右半边只留三行说明。之后是 Look 序列：吊着前轮的二手车、周四夜骑的一句话、门口气泵和手编轮组的细节。强调色全页只用三次：金色的"2"、LOOK 01 的深红底、金色的电话号码。 ### 03 · 票根 Ticket stub `a4906350+1` · 版式 Oversized card ticket · 字体 Bevan / Old Standard TT · 配色 Buff railway card · 语气 田野笔记 · 变数 首屏无按钮 · [brief](briefs/03-ticket-stub.md) 首屏是一张巨大的硬卡火车票：自"河西路"一支红箭头指向"二号桥单车铺"，绿色等级带写着"修车 · 二手车 · 零件 / 不卖新车"，票价格里是补胎、换内胎、保养和免费打气；右侧存根是营业时间，日期章斜盖在角上。票背面拆成甲联到庚联的各种副券：发售条件、价目表、时刻表、夜骑车票和预约联，底纹是 SVG 画的防伪花纹。 ### 04 · 游戏说明书 Game manual `40257aad` · 版式 Strategy-guide spread · 字体 Press Start 2P / Chakra Petch · 配色 Title-screen black · 语气 问答访谈 · 变数 分节编号 · [brief](briefs/04-game-manual.md) 8-bit 攻略本：首屏是像素画的二号桥夜景，桥洞下是半开的蓝色卷帘门、门口的旧车轮和气泵，下方是带"老陈"名牌的对话框，按 ▼ 或 A 键逐条说出事实。后面是 WORLD 1-2 地图（河西路、江、夜骑路线）、1-3 攻略、1-4 数值（价格条以 ¥480 为满格，老陈状态栏 LV 27 = 修车 27 年）和 1-5 秘密：门口 24 小时免费气泵。 ### 05 · 老黄历 Chinese almanac `67d7ad96+1` · 版式 Tear-off day sheet · 字体 Limelight / Cormorant Garamond · 配色 Celadon poster · 语气 配方步骤 · 变数 粗线分区 · [brief](briefs/05-chinese-almanac.md) 一页木刻版式的老黄历：表头是一周七天，周一、周二盖着红色"休"字；中间版心两侧是巨大的"忌"和"宜"，各领一列八条事项和价格。往后每一张撕页的大日期数字都来自事实：180 元、5 天、480 元、90 天保修、24 公里、27 年。每张下半部分按菜谱写法拆成配料、做法、火候和小贴士，章节之间用粗细双线分隔。事实里没有年份和月份，所以表头只写星期。 ## 文件 ``` facts.md 事实清单（唯一允许出现在页面上的内容） roll.json / ROLL.md 5 个哈希、映射、约束、每份 brief 的 JSON briefs/ 5 份冻结 brief previews/ 5 个预览页 compare.html 并排对比页 screenshots/ 每个预览的桌面首屏 / 整页 / 手机，对比页（桌面、手机宽度） ``` 截图用 `npm run screenshots` 生成（需要先 `npx playwright install chromium`）。[`packages/core/test/examples.test.ts`](../../packages/core/test/examples.test.ts) 保证这里的 roll、brief 和 critique 分数与当前数据一致。

# Example: Causeway A full hash-design run for an English-language event page: Causeway, a one-day music festival on an island that you can only walk to at low tide. The festival, the island, the artists and the numbers are fictional; the facts are in [facts.md](facts.md). - **Live compare page:** (press 1–5 to zoom, D/M to switch desktop/mobile) - **All examples:** ![Causeway: five rolled directions side by side](screenshots/compare.png) ## Process 1. **Roll.** The fixed seed only makes the example reproducible; leave `--seed` out in real use. ```bash npm run build node packages/core/dist/bin.js roll --subject "Causeway — a music festival on Skerrow Island" \ --facts-file examples/causeway-festival/facts.md --seed causeway-festival-6 \ --out examples/causeway-festival ``` The MCP equivalent, `roll_designs { subject, facts, seed: "causeway-festival-6", out_dir }`, returns the same five refs. `npm run example:roll -- causeway-festival` runs the same command from the list in [`scripts/examples.mjs`](../../scripts/examples.mjs). **Why `-6`:** the seed rule for the examples is to try ``, `-2`, `-3`, … and keep the first seed whose five branches appear in no earlier example. `causeway-festival` rolled risograph duotone (used by the bakery) and gallery catalogue (used by Sluice); `-2`, `-3` and `-5` also overlapped the bakery or Sluice, and `-4` was clean against those two but shared Swiss grid and Chinese almanac with Bridge No.2. `-6` was the first clean seed. This only keeps the four examples apart; in real use, **don't re-roll because you dislike a result**. 2. **Freeze.** The roll writes [roll.json](roll.json), [ROLL.md](ROLL.md) and [briefs/](briefs). From here on the briefs are fixed specs. 3. **Render.** Following step 3 of the [Skill](../../skills/hash-design/SKILL.md), each preview was built by its own sub-agent that could not see the others. Each one read only its brief and `facts.md`, wrote one self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and SVG, no images, no frameworks), and checked itself with the critique and Playwright screenshots at least twice. In review, #1 was sent back once to remove a "mainland" label and a compass direction that the facts don't give. 4. **Critique.** `npm run example:critique -- causeway-festival`, or per page `hash-design critique previews/NN-*.html --roll roll.json --pick N`: | # | Branch | critique | brief adherence | Minor findings kept | | --- | ------------------ | -------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1 | Engineering plate | 96 | 100 | parts-list sub-items 6.1–6.4 and 7.1–7.4 (one per act) | | 2 | Topographic map | 96 | 100 | margin grid figures, six-figure grid references, legend numbers, the 1:25 000 scale | | 3 | Warm handmade | 100 | 100 | — | | 4 | Editorial magazine | 96 | 100 | accession number "2027.4" (the 2027 edition, the fourth year) | | 5 | Memphis pop | 100 | 100 | — | No critical or major findings. Every minor finding is the "number not in the facts" check firing on numbering that the genre or the brief asks for. 5. **Compare.** `hash-design compare --roll examples/causeway-festival/roll.json` writes [compare.html](compare.html). For an English roll the page's labels are English. 6. **Pick.** The Skill stops here and waits for the user to reply with a number. The example ends here. ## The five directions ### 01 · Engineering plate `c7893950` · layout Exploded assembly · type Architects Daughter / IBM Plex Sans Condensed · palette Drafting vellum · voice field notes · twist vertical text once · [brief](briefs/01-engineering-plate.md) The festival as a drawing sheet with zones 1–8 and A–F: a plan of the island and the 1.2 km causeway with the emergency boat route as a hidden line, sections A–A and B–B, and an enlarged detail of the wet sand and seaweed with boot prints. Levels and the causeway's width are drawn as empty dimensions because the facts don't give them. Revision D stands for the fourth year, and red revision clouds mark the crossing windows. "CAUSEWAY" runs up the left edge, the page's one piece of vertical text. Below come an exploded view with a parts list of stages and acts, a time dimension, the notes and a title block with empty signature boxes. ### 02 · Topographic map `ffc2f9c1` · layout Legend-led · type Barlow Condensed / Barlow · palette Cyanotype field copy · voice dictionary entry · twist accent rationed · [brief](briefs/02-topographic-map.md) A survey sheet in cyanotype blue: the island in contours that never cross, "CAUSEWAY" set along the slope, the Boathouse, the Field and both kitchens, and a 1:25 000 scale bar against which the causeway is drawn exactly 1.2 km long. The tide windows are a scale bar of hours. Every block is a dictionary entry ("Cause·way _n._"), and the yellow survey crayon is used exactly three times: the loop round the Field, the locator outline and its own legend sample. The legend says plainly that heights are not given on this sheet. ### 03 · Warm handmade `ee7a4e44+1` · layout Kraft bag · type Caveat / Alegreya Sans · palette Chalkboard · voice almanac · twist giant glyph · [brief](briefs/03-warm-handmade.md) Paper goods pinned to a chalkboard. The first screen is a speckled rubber stamp with a linocut of the causeway leading to the island, and a giant chalk "C" with a paper tag hanging from it by twine ("one day, one island, one way over"). The back of the bag lists the contents (both line-ups, "net contents: 900 people"), hangs the crossing times as tags on a line, and gives almanac-style "Favourable / Unfavourable" lists ("Boots." / "Your good shoes. See: boots."). A seal sticker carries the Skerrow Island Trust. ### 04 · Editorial magazine `90fa12c0+1` · layout Opening spread · type Bodoni Moda / Libre Baskerville · palette Weekly white · voice museum label · twist zero shadows · [brief](briefs/04-editorial-magazine.md) A magazine feature opening across a spread: _Causeway_ in Bodoni italic over a heavy "2027", a framed museum label ("Medium: Music on two stages; tide; wet sand; seaweed"), a standfirst, the byline "By the Skerrow Island Trust · Photographs: none on file" and a red drop cap. "Continued overleaf" turns the page around the spine. Later spreads carry a navy line drawing of the causeway with a scale bar, a timeline of the day, the line-up as a checklist sidebar and the ticket table. Nothing on the page casts a shadow. ### 05 · Memphis pop `0a75884f+2` · layout Pattern patchwork · type Chango / Questrial · palette Laminate yellow · voice interview Q&A · twist vertical text once · [brief](briefs/05-memphis-pop.md) A patchwork of laminate patterns (grid, squiggles, terrazzo, polka dots, waves) with hard black edges. A white title panel overlaps it: "Causeway" in Chango with a red squiggle underline, a green disc and a red triangle. The date runs down a green strip, the one piece of vertical text. Everything is a Q&A answered by the Skerrow Island Trust, from the crossing windows to the enamel cup, and a to-scale tide timeline marks the 21:45 last set. Hovering a patch steps it through other patterns. ## Files ``` facts.md the fact sheet (the only content a page may state) roll.json / ROLL.md the five hashes, mapping, constraints and each brief as JSON briefs/ five frozen briefs previews/ five preview pages compare.html side-by-side compare page screenshots/ desktop first screen / full page / mobile per preview, compare page (desktop and phone width) ``` Screenshots come from `npm run screenshots` (run `npx playwright install chromium` first). # Architecture / 设计机制

[中文首页](../README.md) · [English](../README.en.md)

## Fixed styles and hash generation

The 21 [fixed styles](presets.md) define stable names, palette roles, fonts, illustrations and website layouts. The browser, CLI and MCP use the same preset lookup. Direct selection uses a stable specification and can be repeated independently of random history.

Hash generation samples those 21 directions plus the original eight. A direction's palette candidates include the compatible [historical hash-design swatches](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), where available. Small shared hue shifts and bounded changes in lightness preserve the source palette relationships. The original directions also sample continuous colour ranges. Actual canvas chroma and text contrast are checked after conversion to sRGB.

## Original procedural directions

The finite building blocks are **operators**, not complete styles. Eight art-direction grammars constrain typography, allowed layouts, colour families, colour relationships, graphic purpose and material. Eleven structured graphic operators construct one subject or one repeat system. The engine samples actual palette colours, layout balance, density, whitespace, typography metrics, meaningful graphic amplitude/count/line weight and surface parameters. Arbitrary rotation and mirrored copies are disabled. It combines these rules under scenario and readability constraints.

These components are intentionally finite and inspectable. The engine does not invent new art movements, generate new font files, or prove that all combinations are perceptually distinct. Continuous parameters expand the space of visual systems; meaningful variety must also be checked across structural attributes.

`src/core/engine.js` is shared by Node, the browser and MCP. It has no model provider, network request or filesystem dependency. `src/core/graphics.js` draws deterministic SVG. `src/render.js` creates the website and brief; `src/pptx.js` exports native PowerPoint text, shapes, table and chart plus SVG artwork.

## Sampling

1. Validate request, including conflicting locks and brand/mode constraints.
2. Create a fresh cryptographic random seed unless one is supplied.
3. Derive a deterministic non-cryptographic PRNG stream from SHA-256 of the versioned seed. This is procedural sampling, not a source of additional entropy.
4. Select a coherent art direction, then generate continuous OKLCH colours within compatible families, font roles, supported spatial relations and meaningful graphic parameters. Default large canvases are chromatic. Materials and graphics must obey the same direction. See [visual-direction.md](visual-direction.md).
5. Check schema, semantic visual fingerprint and selected text contrast. Typography uses real referenced fonts and CJK fallback families.
6. Within each block of 24 candidates, rank valid candidates by minimum distance, recent direction frequency and light/dark diversity. Reject candidates below the requested threshold and continue until the set is complete or the attempt budget is exhausted.

## Novelty policy

- **Exact visual identity:** SHA-256 over canonical visual parameters only. Names, content, timestamps and selection seed do not make a style unique. SVG seed participates only for operators whose geometry actually uses it; unused count/rotation/seed fields are excluded.
- **Recent similarity:** weighted attribute distance (0–1), using art direction, actual canvas hue/lightness/chroma, colour family, font family/category, composition, graphic family, density, type scale, spatial balance, amplitude, texture and depth. Default minimum: 0.22. Recent window: 40 shown themes. Candidate budget: 1,400. These are explicit v0.2 defaults, not a runtime fallback to weaker constraints.
- **All history vs recent:** exact fingerprints are checked against all retained entries; similarity is checked against the last 40 by default. Related visual languages may reappear outside that window. This directly targets infrequent recurrence rather than a promise of infinite global uniqueness.
- **Failure:** no silent relaxation. The caller receives an exhaustion error; no partial set is added to history.
- **History scope:** Node defaults to `~/.random-design/history-v2.json` with a process lock and atomic file replacement. Browser uses localStorage and Web Locks when available; without Web Locks, concurrent tabs are not fully serialized. Export/import transfers history between environments. HTTP MCP receives client-owned history; it has no cross-user ledger.

The distance measure compares specified attributes. The rendered catalogue provides the visual review surface. Fixed styles and hashed variants share the same exporters.

## Reproduction and content

The authoritative artifact is `design.json`, not a seed. History affects which candidates a run accepts. Store JSON and the matching release/rule fingerprint to reproduce a visual specification. Content is supplied separately. The engine does not randomize factual text, numbers or voice. The built-in sample and chart values are clearly fictional. The native exporter is a six-slide theme specimen; users/agents should adapt actual content and review all slides. Long custom content is subject to layout review; the sample exporter is not a semantic slide-layout optimizer.

`random-design/3` identifies the v0.3 sampling rules. `LIBRARY` hashes the declarative pools. v0.3 reads the v0.2 saved specifications and history entries. Use the release matching the stored seed if you need to reconstruct a previous sampling sequence from the seed.

# Visual direction / 视觉规则

v0.2.0 is an art-direction revision. Its acceptance criterion is a coherent rendered design, not a large count of different parameter hashes.

## The problem in v0.1

Backgrounds were sampled at almost-white or almost-black lightness with very little chroma. Most visual difference lived in the accent colour. Fonts, graphics and layouts were selected independently. Graphic operators could then receive a mirrored or rotated translucent duplicate. This produced numerous specifications with weak visual differences and unmotivated ornament.

## The v0.2 hierarchy

1. Choose a visual language with a concrete material/graphic logic.
2. Choose colours from that language's allowed colour families, then generate actual continuous OKLCH values. A coloured ground is a major area, not an accent swatch.
3. Select compatible font roles, a supported spatial arrangement and a graphic with a defined purpose.
4. Construct one subject or one repeat system. Generate its meaningful internal parameters; do not pile unrelated shapes on top.
5. Apply the corresponding material treatment and render it on web and PowerPoint.
6. Compare the actual outputs for hierarchy, coherence, graphic purpose, colour-area balance, content fit and craft. Rule and distance checks remain engineering checks only.

## Current visual grammars

| Grammar | Graphic purpose | Relationships that must hold |
|---|---|---|
| Colour edition / 套色版画 | One print emblem | Two inks on coloured stock, limited registration offset, forceful display type |
| Paper atelier / 剪纸工坊 | One cut-paper study | Three connected paper forms, paper edge/shadow, a caption block |
| Enamel sign / 珐琅招牌 | Name and sign frame | Main typography, nested border and one small ornament; no competing hero illustration |
| Botanical folio / 植物图鉴 | One specimen-like plant | Alternating tapered leaves attached to the exact same curved stem, fine veins and a plate border; not a botanical identification claim |
| Cyanotype study / 蓝晒图纸 | One constructed form | Blue/cyan colour range, projection lines that refer to the same object, precise type and grid |
| Woven rhythm / 织物图样 | A coherent repeat | One warp/weft or tile unit, consistent direction and selvedge |
| Editorial colour / 艺术刊物 | Typography as image | Large editorial title, columns/rules and one secondary publisher-style mark |
| Constructed play / 几何游乐 | A modular composition | A shared axis, limited geometric units, strong colour relationships |

These are finite curated grammars, not eight magically unlimited art movements. Continuous colours, proportions, type metrics, meaningful graphic parameters and alternative compatible arrangements produce variants. Expanding meaningful visual variety requires designing and reviewing additional grammars, not multiplying random numbers.

## Colour-area policy

The default `rich` mode samples twelve chromatic canvas families. Lightness and chroma ranges deliberately avoid near-white and near-black defaults. Different colour families are used within an unconstrained five-direction set. `balanced` can include neutral stocks; `neutral` explicitly requests a restrained ground. The separate light/dark preference controls luminance, not whether the canvas is colourful.

Text colour is selected for its actual background. `panelInk` is checked against `panel`, in addition to main-text, secondary-text and button pairs. Readability constraints do not require a black/white canvas.

Auxiliary colours obey direction-specific relationships. A botanical plate uses sage foliage and a warm seed ink; a cyanotype uses related linework and one ochre annotation ink; an enamel sign uses one warm sign ink for its ornament; a woven study uses related yarn colours. The palette is not a set of unrelated independently sampled swatches.

## Validation limits

Regression tests check actual canvas chroma/lightness and compatible type/graphic/material choices. They cannot decide whether a design is elegant. Screenshots and actual PPTX renders are therefore the primary review artifacts. No benchmark count or generated ID should be presented as evidence of beautiful, original or human-distinct styles.

# Contributing to hash-design

Thanks for your interest! Bug reports, new design branches, better critique rules, documentation and translations are all welcome. By participating you agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

[中文摘要](#中文摘要)

## Ground rules

- **Do not let the model choose the style.** The project exists to take aesthetic choice away from the agent. Features that let an agent override a rolled direction "because it looks better" will not be accepted.
- **No invented facts.** Examples, fixtures and docs must not contain fake testimonials, user counts or logos.
- **Keep the CLI and the MCP server in parity.** Every MCP tool has a CLI equivalent, and both go through the core's public API.
- **Docs must match the code.** If you change a parameter, a flag, a tool or a default, update the docs in the same pull request.

## Development setup

Requires Node.js ≥ 20; `.nvmrc` pins 22.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design.git
cd hash-design
npm install
npm run build
npm run check   # typecheck + lint + prettier --check + vitest
node scripts/smoke.mjs
```

| Script                          | What it does                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run build`                 | `tsc -b` for both packages                                                                    |
| `npm test`                      | Vitest (core, CLI, MCP over in-memory transport, sync and example checks)                     |
| `npm run check`                 | Everything CI checks except the smoke test and pack dry-run                                   |
| `npm run format`                | Prettier `--write`                                                                            |
| `npm run sync`                  | Regenerate `SKILL.md`'s bans block, its `.claude/` / `.cursor/` copies and `docs/branches.md` |
| `node scripts/smoke.mjs`        | CLI + MCP server over real stdio                                                              |
| `node scripts/verify-fonts.mjs` | Check every Google Fonts URL online (not run in CI)                                           |
| `npm run examples`              | List the example runs and their seeds (`scripts/examples.mjs`)                                |
| `npm run example:roll`          | Re-roll every example with its fixed seed (`-- <name>` for one)                               |
| `npm run example:critique`      | Critique every example preview against its brief; fails below 90                              |
| `npm run example:compare`       | Rebuild every example's `compare.html`                                                        |
| `npm run screenshots`           | Playwright screenshots of every example (`npx playwright install chromium` first)             |
| `npm run hero`                  | Rebuild `docs/assets/hero.png` and `social-preview.png` from the example screenshots          |
| `npm run hero:gif`              | Rebuild the animated `docs/assets/hero.gif` and `hero.mp4` (needs ffmpeg)                     |

The code layout is described in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), and the mapping algorithm in [docs/mapping.md](docs/mapping.md).

## Pull requests

1. Fork, then create a branch from `main`.
2. Make focused commits using [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) as the history does: `feat(core): …`, `fix(mcp): …`, `docs: …`, `test: …`, `ci: …`, `chore: …`.
3. Run `npm run check` and `node scripts/smoke.mjs` locally.
4. Add an entry under `## [Unreleased]` in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for user-visible changes.
5. Open the pull request and fill in the template. CI must be green on Node 20, 22 and 24.

## Adding or changing a design branch

Branches are the heart of the project, and the most valuable contribution. A good branch is a **real-world design genre** with references you can point to (a printed artifact, a signage system, a historical movement), not a mood ("modern", "clean", "playful").

1. Open a [new branch proposal](https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design/issues/new?template=branch_proposal.yml) first if you want feedback before writing it.
2. Write the branch in `packages/core/src/data/branches/`, at the level of detail of `_exemplar.ts` (`supermarket-circular`): bilingual name and concept, at least 2 references, at least 3 keywords, tokens, 3 options for each of layouts, type, palettes, motion, motifs, anchors and surfaces, 1–3 densities and scales, and must / must-not lists.
3. Add its id to `BRANCH_ORDER` in `packages/core/src/data/branches/index.ts`. Keep each family spread evenly around the order, because the collision walk depends on it (see [mapping.md §4](docs/mapping.md#4-branch-order)).
4. Run the checks. `npm test` runs the validator, which enforces:
   - ink/paper contrast ≥ 7:1 and muted/paper ≥ 4.5:1, plus at least one light palette
   - lowercase `#rrggbb` values and no framework default colours (`FRAMEWORK_DEFAULT_HEX`)
   - no banned fonts, including in fallbacks
   - a display family leads at most 3 branches
   - no two branches share the same lead palette (paper + accent)
5. Run `node scripts/verify-fonts.mjs` so every Google Fonts URL resolves.
6. Run `npm run sync` to regenerate `docs/branches.md` and the Skill's generated block.
7. **Re-roll the examples** (next section). Any data change alters the library fingerprint, and `examples.test.ts` will fail until you do.

## Re-rolling the examples after a data change

The four runs under `examples/` (`fourth-lane-bakery`, `sluice`, `bridge-two-bikes`, `causeway-festival`, listed in [`scripts/examples.mjs`](scripts/examples.mjs)) are pinned to the library fingerprint. After changing branches, pools or bans:

1. `npm run build && npm run example:roll` rewrites every `roll.json`, `ROLL.md` and `briefs/`. If two examples now share a branch, `examples.test.ts` fails: move the later example to the next free seed (`<name>-2`, `<name>-3`, …) in `scripts/examples.mjs`.
2. Render one preview per brief following the [Skill](skills/hash-design/SKILL.md), step 3: each preview is produced from **its own brief only** (separate agent sessions), as a single self-contained HTML file in `previews/NN-<branch>.html`.
3. `npm run example:critique` must pass: every preview scores at least 90 with no critical or major findings (`examples.test.ts` checks the same).
4. `npm run example:compare`, then `npm run screenshots`, then `npm run hero` and `npm run hero:gif` (the README hero images and the social preview are built from `examples/causeway-festival`).
5. Update everything that quotes the examples: the demo sections of every `README*.md`, each example's `README.md`, `examples/index.html`, and the worked examples and fingerprint in `docs/mapping.md` / `docs/mapping.zh-CN.md`.

If that is more than you can take on, say so in the pull request; a maintainer can help with the re-roll.

## Changing the critique rules

Rules live in `packages/core/src/critique.ts`. Add or adjust a fixture under `packages/core/test/fixtures/` and a test in `critique.test.ts` that shows the rule firing on bad input and staying quiet on good input. Keep the rule ids in sync with the bans in `packages/core/src/data/bans.ts`, then run `npm run sync`.

## Changing MCP tools or CLI flags

Update, in the same pull request: the tool schema in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`, the CLI in `packages/core/src/cli.ts` (including `--help`), the tests, [docs/mcp-tools.md](docs/mcp-tools.md) and its Chinese version, the tool tables in all `README*.md` files, and the MCP ↔ CLI table in `skills/hash-design/SKILL.md` (then `npm run sync`).

- `README.md` (English) is the source of truth. `README.zh-CN.md`, `README.ja.md`, `README.ko.md` and `README.es.md` are translations.
- When you change the English README, update the translations if you can. If you cannot, open an issue so a translator can follow up, and mention it in the pull request.
- Keep code blocks, commands, package names, tool names and flags identical across languages; only prose and comments are translated.

Use the [issue templates](https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design/issues/new/choose). For security problems, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and do not open a public issue.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

hash-design has not been published to npm yet. Security fixes are made on the `main` branch; once releases exist, the latest minor version will receive fixes.

| Version        | Supported |
| -------------- | --------- |
| `main` / 0.1.x | yes       |

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not open a public issue** for security problems.

Report privately through GitHub: go to the repository's **Security** tab and click **Report a vulnerability** ([direct link](https://github.com/qybaihe/hash-design/security/advisories/new)). Private vulnerability reporting is enabled for this repository.

Include what you can of the following:

- the affected component (core library, CLI, MCP server, Skill, example pages)
- the version or commit
- steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept
- the impact you expect

You should get an acknowledgement within 7 days. Once a fix is ready, it will be released with a GitHub Security Advisory crediting you, unless you prefer to stay anonymous.

## Threat model

Knowing what the code does helps decide whether something is a vulnerability:

- **Local only.** The CLI and the MCP server run on your machine with your user's permissions. The MCP server speaks stdio only; it opens no network ports and makes no network requests.
- **Filesystem access.** `roll_designs` (with `out_dir`) and `build_compare_page` write files; `critique_page` (`path`, `roll_path`) and `build_compare_page` (`roll_path`) read files. Paths are resolved against the server's working directory and are not sandboxed: an MCP client, or a model driving it, can ask the server to read or write any path your user can access. Only connect hash-design to clients and agents you trust, and review tool calls if your client allows it.
- **Untrusted HTML.** `critique_page` parses HTML and CSS with `node-html-parser` and regular expressions. It never executes scripts or loads remote resources. Crashes or pathological slowness on crafted input are in scope.
- **Generated pages.** Briefs and previews reference Google Fonts, so opening a generated page in a browser makes requests to `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com`. The compare page embeds previews in iframes from the same directory.
- **Randomness.** Real rolls use `crypto.randomBytes`. Rolls are not secrets: the hashes are design seeds, not credentials, and `seed` is deliberately predictable.

Out of scope: problems that need an already-compromised machine or a malicious MCP client that you configured yourself, and the design quality of generated pages.

# Material and reference guide

The 21 presets are original implementations informed by the user's reference video. The video is not redistributed. Their material treatment was rebuilt in v0.4.0. These are reference-informed adaptations, not pixel-identical copies of the source video.

Preserve the user's content. Apply a style through composition, type, material and a meaningful subject. A coffee cup belongs in the sample cafe, not automatically in a scientific or business deck.

| Style | Material and compositional requirement |
|---|---|
| Cyberpunk | Dark field, luminous outlines, controlled RGB title displacement, three signal-coloured menu cards. |
| Retro Terminal | Deep green CRT field, fine scanlines, compact monospaced information, thin rules. |
| Skeuomorphism | Warm directional wood grain, inset green menu board, pinned paper tags, ceramic rims and contact shadows. |
| Glassmorphism | Background colour remains visible through translucent panels; rim highlights and one soft shadow establish thickness. |
| Brutalism | Large compressed type, hard borders and decisive yellow/red information blocks. |
| Pop Art | Halftone printing, outlined lettering, speech-label copy and comic price stamps; illustration supports the product. |
| Memphis | Asymmetric, bounded rhythm using circles, waves and triangles; maintain a clear title and menu. |
| Editorial | Large serif title, fine column rules, numbered entries, quiet paper and a single circular image. |
| Swiss Style | Strict alignment, strong typographic hierarchy, spare red mark, unboxed menu rows. |
| Claymorphism | Rounded volumes with broad diffuse highlights, warm contact shadows and pastel raised cards. |
| Neumorphism | Same-colour substrate, raised and recessed rims, top-left light, paired light/dark edge shadows. |
| Y2K | Iridescent surface, chrome/gloss highlights, capsule controls and a slim desktop-window frame. |
| Pixel Art | Consistent pixel grid, integer edges, legible game-like counter scene and stepped outlines. |
| Neubrutalism | Thick outlines, offset hard shadows and independent bright cards; avoid unrelated ornaments. |
| Bauhaus | Primary-colour geometry describes one composition; circles, rectangles and triangles align to a grid. |
| Vaporwave | Sunset horizon, perspective grid and translucent retro window cards. |
| Aurora Gradient | Tall luminous curtains fade into a dark ground; quiet centred title and translucent lower cards. |
| Art Deco | Restrained brass lines, symmetric fan, stepped frames and centred hierarchy. |
| Sci-Fi HUD | Concentric instrument marks, technical rules, restrained cyan emission and amber readings. |
| Bento Grid | Unequal tiles, strong dominant block, consistent gutters and individual content roles. |
| New Chinese Style | Short vertical calligraphic title, layered landscape within a round window, paper field and restrained vermilion seal. |

Use one light direction across the subject, frame and cards. Highlights describe a rim or volume; shadows describe contact or elevation. Check rendered output at full size and at thumbnail scale. Check headings, prices, body copy and overflow on mobile. Colour-token contrast validation does not prove contrast on every translucent or gradient surface.

Websites use CSS surfaces and original SVG artwork. PowerPoint uses native text, tables and charts with SVG substrates and illustrations. Preserve those editable objects. Verify exported PPTX separately; browser CSS blur is not a native PowerPoint effect. The renderer's transparent SVG gradient stops produced black shadow disks during review; layered translucent shapes are used for portable contact shadows.

The sampling algorithm remains random-design/3. Renderer revision material/1 belongs to v0.4.0. Save JSON and the release: old JSON is still accepted, but opening it in this release adopts the new renderer. Use the original release for an exact old rendering. Fixed selection remains stable; random history is not consumed by selecting a fixed preset.

1. Inspect the complete examples in https://xingchenyd.github.io/random-design/showcase/.
2. Obtain 3–5 briefs with generate_reference_briefs. Pass subject, facts, language and count. Preserve supplied wording and data. Use include with count 1 for an explicit direction; use exclude for recently used IDs.

### `packages/mcp` (`hash-design-mcp`)

A thin adapter over the core's public API using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` input schemas. Every tool has a CLI equivalent, and a test checks that `roll_designs` with the example seed returns exactly the refs of the CLI-generated example roll. See [mcp-tools.md](mcp-tools.md).

Design choices:

- **Flat constraint parameters** (`light_only`, `brand_colors`, …) rather than a nested object: models fill flat schemas more reliably.
- **Two content blocks** from `roll_designs`: Markdown for the model to read and a small JSON block for programmatic clients.
- **`detail: summary` by default when `out_dir` is set**, so five full briefs do not flood the context; the agent then reads each brief file on its own, which is what keeps previews independent.
- Tool annotations mark `get_brief`, `list_branches`, `get_branch` and `critique_page` as read-only.

## Data as code

Branches are TypeScript objects, not YAML or JSON, so the compiler checks their shape and the validator can run in tests. Each branch carries:

- id, bilingual name and concept, references, keywords, family
- tokens (grid, radius, border, shadow policy)
- 3 options for each of layouts, type pairings, palettes, motion, motifs, anchors and surfaces
- 1–3 allowed densities and modular scales
- must / must-not lists

`validateLibrary` (run in `branches.test.ts`) enforces: 3–5 options per dimension, lowercase `#rrggbb` hex, ink/paper ≥ 7:1 and muted/paper ≥ 4.5:1 contrast, at least one light palette, no banned fonts (fallbacks included), no framework default hex values, a display family leading at most 3 branches, unique ids and names. `branches.test.ts` also checks that no two branches share the same lead palette (paper + accent). `scripts/verify-fonts.mjs` checks every Google Fonts URL online (235/235); it is not in CI because it needs the network.

# Sluice · fact sheet (example; the product, people and numbers are fictional)
# Only these facts may appear on the page. One per line; lines starting with "#" are comments.

- Name: Sluice — a self-hosted inbox for webhooks
- What it does: gives you a public URL for webhooks, stores every delivery, and forwards it to your local or internal service
- One static binary, about 11 MB, for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64
- Storage: a single SQLite file; no Redis, no Postgres, no queue to run
- Install: curl -fsSL https://sluice.example/install.sh | sh
- Start: sluice serve --forward http://localhost:3000
- Retries failed forwards with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours
- Replay any stored delivery: sluice replay <delivery-id>
- Verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures and rejects deliveries older than 5 minutes
- Web UI on port 8081: search deliveries by path, header or body text
- Keeps deliveries for 30 days by default; change it with --retain
- 1,800 deliveries per second on a 2-vCPU VM, in the project's own benchmark
- No hosted service, no account, no telemetry
- Written in Go; MIT licence; 41 contributors
- Current version 0.9.2, released 14 October 2026
- Maintainer: Ines Okafor, who started it in 2023 after losing a weekend of payment webhooks
